topic: A small print shop invites first-timers to make a zine. Inkspot Press and Juno Park are a made-up example.

slides.title: Make a zine in two days
slides.subtitle: Eight pages, one sheet of paper, no budget.

slides.title: Why zines are back
slides.body: A feed scrolls past. A zine stays on a shelf. Small print runs let you share work that is too weird, too personal or too slow for an algorithm.

slides.title: What you need
items: One sheet of paper, folded into eight pages
A pen, scissors and a photocopier
Something you care about more than likes

slides.label: zines printed in our shop by first-timers
slides.note: Most of them were made in a single weekend.

slides.quote: Nobody asked for my zine about bus stops. Forty people took a copy anyway.
slides.author: Juno Park

slides.title: Fold, cut, staple
slides.caption: One sheet becomes an eight-page booklet in three minutes.

slides.title: Make one this weekend
slides.text: Eight pages, one evening, no rules. The first copy is the hardest.
